summary: In this episode, Father Andrew reads the full text of the Harrowing of Hell from the Gospel of Nicodemus (Acts of Pilate), an apocryphal New Testament text from the 4th-5th century. He explains that this text belongs to the category of books to be read at home, not Scripture, but is honored in Orthodox liturgical tradition. The narrative describes the descent of Christ into Hades after his crucifixion, where he breaks the gates of brass, defeats Satan and Death, and leads the righteous dead—including Adam, the patriarchs, and prophets—out of hell and into Paradise. The reading includes the testimony of the two sons of Simeon, Karinus and Leucius, who were raised from the dead and recount the events. The episode concludes with the saints entering Paradise, the appearance of Enoch, Elijah, and the penitent thief, and the return of the witnesses to Jerusalem.

entities.title: Jesus Christ
entities.summary: The central figure of Christianity, who descends into hell and rescues the righteous dead.

entities.title: Adam
entities.summary: The first man, who is rescued from hell by Christ.

entities.title: Satan
entities.summary: The prince of death who opposes Christ but is defeated and bound in hell.

entities.title: Hell (personified)
entities.summary: Personified as a character who argues with Satan and is forced to release the dead.

entities.title: David
entities.summary: The prophet and king who prophesies Christ's victory over death.

entities.title: Isaiah
entities.summary: The prophet who foretold the light shining on those in darkness.

entities.title: John the Baptist
entities.summary: The forerunner of Christ who announces his arrival in hell.

entities.title: Seth
entities.summary: Son of Adam who recounts the prophecy of Michael about the oil of mercy.

entities.title: Michael the Archangel
entities.summary: The angel who delivers Adam to Paradise and gives instructions to the witnesses.

entities.title: Enoch
entities.summary: One of the two witnesses who were taken to Paradise without dying.

entities.title: Elijah
entities.summary: The prophet taken up in a chariot of fire, who will return before the end.

entities.title: Penitent Thief
entities.summary: The robber crucified with Jesus who was promised Paradise and enters with the sign of the cross.

entities.title: Karinus and Leucius
entities.summary: The two sons of Simeon who were raised from the dead and wrote the account of the Harrowing of Hell.

entities.title: Joseph of Arimathea

entities.title: Annas and Caiaphas

entities.title: Nicodemus
entities.summary: A Pharisee who helps Joseph and receives the writings of Leucius.

entities.title: Pontius Pilate

concepts.title: Harrowing of Hell
concepts.summary: The descent of Christ into Hades after his death to rescue the righteous dead, a key event in Christian theology.

concepts.title: Gospel of Nicodemus
concepts.summary: An apocryphal text from the 4th-5th century, also known as the Acts of Pilate, containing traditions about Christ's descent into hell.

concepts.title: Books Read at Home
concepts.summary: A category of Christian literature that is not Scripture but is edifying for private reading, distinct from heretical texts.

claims.text: The Gospel of Nicodemus is not Scripture but a book to be read at home, reflecting traditions not in the Bible.
The ancient church distinguished three categories: books read in church (Scripture), books read at home, and books not to be read (heretical).
Christ, as King of Glory, tramples death, binds Satan, and leads the righteous dead out of hell.
Michael the Archangel told Seth that after 5500 years, the Son of God would come to anoint believers with the oil of mercy through baptism.
Christ makes the sign of the cross over Adam and the saints, and the penitent thief uses the sign to enter Paradise.
